Rule_Name: Topology-Sensitive Workloads Must Match the Server PCIe and Device Locality Topology
Rule_Description: If the workload is sensitive to GPU-to-CPU, GPU-to-NIC, GPU-to-NVMe, or multi-GPU communication locality, the candidate server configuration must provide verified topology information and satisfy the applicable placement/locality requirements; if the topology cannot be verified, the decision must remain INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE rather than assuming an equivalent topology.
Inputs: Workload topology sensitivity; PCIe_Configuration; PCIe_Slots; PCIe_Lane_Availability; PCIe_PCIe_Network_Interface; CPU_GPU_Interconnect; GPU_Interconnect; GPU_Configuration_GPU_Form_Factor; NUMA topology evidence; GPU-NIC topology evidence
Input_Source: AI SERVER(5).CSV + NVIDIA-Certified Systems Configuration Guide
Condition: Topology-sensitive workload requires a specific or performance-relevant device locality/topology AND candidate server topology is verified and satisfies the applicable locality requirement
Output_Decision: FEASIBLE only when the required topology/locality is verified; otherwise INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE
Source_Title: AI SERVER(5).CSV — Project Server Hardware Catalogue; NVIDIA-Certified Systems Configuration Guide
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: NVIDIA guide: Introduction; Application Considerations—Workload Sizing; Table 1 Inference Server System; Table 2 Deep Learning Training System; PCIe Topology; lines 55–56, 121–136, 152–167
Evidence: NVIDIA states that optimal PCIe server configurations depend on the target workload and vary case-by-case. Its inference and training configurations specify balanced GPU distribution across CPU sockets and PCIe root ports and place NIC/NVMe devices under the same PCIe switch or root complex as the GPUs. The project catalogue contains PCIe and interconnect descriptors but lacks a complete structured topology map, so topology-sensitive decisions require verification rather than inference.
Applicability: Topology-sensitive single-server AI workloads and multi-GPU configurations where CPU/GPU/NIC/NVMe locality or PCIe topology can affect the intended workload. Applies to training and inference when the workload's communication/data-movement pattern makes locality material.
Limitations: NVIDIA's recommendations are configuration guidance, not a universal performance threshold. The catalogue does not contain a complete structured PCIe/NUMA/GPU-NIC topology map. The rule therefore gates evidence sufficiency and configuration matching; it does not predict a universal performance gain or impose a universal GPU/socket ratio.
Validation_Status: Validated as a new server-level integration rule; no duplicate found among SRV-001–SRV-028.
